A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CLiViS work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable, including the image-based qualitative examples. Relocated content and actual omissions can be distinguished reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations on OpenEQA, EgoTempo and EgoSchema, component ablations, reasoning-dynamics analysis and qualitative results.

after.justification: v2 retains original evaluations and adds baseline comparisons, component ablations, latency measurements and frontier-model experiments.

M1.justification: The training-free LLM–VLM pipeline, cognitive-map and evidence-memory components, and stopping procedure are retained. Section 3.3 expands the description of conflict resolution, temporal precedence and atomic updates, but does not establish a changed underlying algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same OpenEQA, EgoSchema and EgoTempo coverage, including the same qualitative case and question categories. Added model configurations and latency measurements introduce no new dataset, task or input scenario.

E2.justification: v2 substantially broadens evaluated comparisons: Table 1 adds AlanaVLM across all three benchmarks and VideoTree participation on OpenEQA and EgoTempo. New Table 6 compares CLiViS against standalone GPT-4.1 and Gemini-2.5-flash, extending comparison to frontier multimodal models.

E3.justification: v2 adds latency measurement on EgoSchema, frontier-model configurations and additional ablation controls. The 21.4% control previously labeled Cognitive Map removal is now labeled Relation Graph removal; this does not establish a rerun. Existing dataset splits, accuracy scoring, preprocessing and iteration limits remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 3 adds targeted tests of Navigation Graph removal and replacing the LLM reasoner with InternVL3. Table 4 adds an accuracy–latency analysis. The existing reasoning-dynamics plot, category analysis and qualitative case are retained, with reasoning dynamics moved to the supplement.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or comparable uncertainty estimates. The retained bubble plot depicts sample frequency and accuracy, not newly introduced uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Existing CLiViS benchmark scores remain unchanged, but substantial results are added. These include VideoTree and AlanaVLM entries, navigation-removal and VLM-reasoner accuracies of 20.6% and 10.6%, and latencies of 71/644/195 seconds for VideoTree/VideoAgent/CLiViS. Table 6 reports standalone/CLiViS accuracies of 34.2/36.8% for GPT-4.1 and 27.4/30.8% for Gemini. Section 4.3 changes the stated average from 48.4% to 49.4%, although the corresponding table value remains 49.3%.

T1.justification: Equations 1–10 and the formal task, graph and evidence-memory definitions are retained. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs; the expanded update explanation adds no formal derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims: training-free linguistic–visual collaboration, a dynamic cognitive map bridging perception and reasoning, and effectiveness across benchmarks and foundation models.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations contrasting iterative verification with VideoTree/LVNet, interprets the new ablation as establishing a dedicated LLM's necessity, and discusses the accuracy–latency tradeoff. It removes Appendix E's specific spatial/temporal hallucination limitations and proposed mitigations. A brief acknowledgment of latency challenges remains in Section 4.6.

D1.justification: v1 Appendix D provides complete stage-specific prompts and output schemas; v2 removes these from the PDF and points to a separate supplementary prompt folder whose contents are not supplied or embedded. v2 adds graph-update implementation explanations, while the existing hyperparameters, preprocessing, Neo4j details, hardware and code link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including ReMEmbR, ObjectRelator, V2-SAM and robotics/driving works, while removing entries including ImageBind, ECBench and EgoPlan-Bench2. The main research positioning remains intact. Consolidating VideoTree's duplicate references and updating publication metadata do not constitute new related works.

P1.justification: The supplementary structure is substantially revised: reasoning dynamics moves from the main text, new comparison and overview sections appear, and the detailed prompt-design, limitations and broader-impact sections disappear. Related-work and method passages are condensed or rewritten, while the main section sequence remains largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column layout with extensive resizing and repositioning. Figure 1's panels are rearranged, Table 3 expands, and new latency and frontier-model tables appear. The category table moves from Table 4 to Table 5; Figure 5 moves to the supplement, while Figures 6–8 retain identical image content.

improvement.justification: The added ablations, latency measurements and frontier-model comparisons strengthen empirical support. However, removing complete prompts and specific hallucination limitations weakens the supplied PDF's reproducibility and qualification of claims. New VideoTree results also contradict retained prose saying those evaluations are omitted, and the revised average remains inconsistent with the table. These material benefits and losses prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
